verification_report.summary:
The entire submitted section passes the independent sequential audit: 19 statement checks and 5 reference/context checks found no critical errors or gaps. This verdict is conditional on the expressly accepted envelope-system retraction and realization criterion from chapter_envelope_systems.tex, under separate audit hermitian_envelope_systems_01. That prerequisite was instantiated, not established circularly.

The lattice action is free and properly discontinuous, giving a connected smooth compact holomorphic P1-bundle. The invariant v and both divisor metrics glue correctly. All three displayed complex Hessian entries and the Schur complement t(1-tr)/(4(1+tr)) are correct. With sigma=sigma0/pi, the lower curvature bound has exactly the claimed constant. At xi=0, the Hessian matrix after adding A times the pulled-back sigma is [[A,i/2],[-i/2,1/t]]: its vertical coefficient is positive and its Schur complement is A-t/4. Thus strict positivity at infinity is verified directly, and kappa is Kähler because t=1 and A=pi. Smooth f_t proves nefness; compact metric comparison supplies f_eta for every positive Hermitian eta, including nonclosed eta.

The periodic-subharmonic argument is valid, including identically minus-infinity restrictions, and proves rigidity without importing DPS rigidity. The quotient and distinguished section match [DPS94 Example 1.7](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/dps1.pdf). Its extension-theorem proof of nefness is not used. Squared norms, ddc=i/(2pi)partial-barpartial, unit Green mass and coefficient-one Poincare-Lelong identities are consistent.

The component envelopes are genuine normalized Q-fixed potentials; their all-weight ideals are O(-floor(t)F), including integer weights. Equality of ideals in the common larger background proves compatibility, and constant slices satisfy every a<c. The passage from all-weight ideals to Lelong numbers is valid after checking the differing weight conventions and I-plus formulation in [Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.00368). The accepted canonical limit retains coefficient at least one on F. Distributional subtraction yields a genuine theta-PSH residual; rigidity gives q=psi_F+psi_D+C. Transversality yields precisely O(-floor(t)(F+D)). Hence recovery fails, E is not surjective, and R is not injective.

For each fixed eta, divisorial removal and the normalized competitor bound make w_eta bounded; no uniform bound as eta tends to zero is needed. For closed eta=epsilon kappa, locality, absence of pluripolar mass and bounded Stokes give exactly the claimed residual intersection mass. The normal bundle of D is trivial, so D squared is zero. In fact, integral theta wedge kappa=1 and integral kappa squared=2, making the mass 2epsilon+2epsilon squared, tending to zero. The limiting current [F]+[D] has zero non-pluripolar product. No bounded mass failure is involved.

The supplied [SGPT source](/Users/mingchen/Non-Kahler/research/sources/SGPT.pdf) was checked directly: its full inverse-system space permits zero volume, while Lemma 13.1.2 characterizes recovery from positive-volume base curves. The closing claim is consistent with this distinction and asserts neither a positive-residual-volume counterexample nor novelty.
